question: Why do most software projects fail to deliver on time and on budget?

expected_sub_questions: What are the most common causes of scope creep?
How does estimation failure contribute to overruns?
What role does team communication play in project failure?
How do external dependencies cause delays?
What does research say about the base rate of software project failure?
key_findings: Requirements change faster than delivery cycles
The Standish CHAOS report consistently shows ~30% outright failure, ~50% challenged
known_answer.likely_contradiction: answers about individual skill vs systemic factors may tension against each other

observe: Did the model decompose into distinct, answerable sub-questions? Did cross-check find the tension between individual and systemic explanations? Is the report headline specific rather than generic?

question: What makes a programming language achieve widespread adoption?

expected_sub_questions: What role does a killer use-case or platform play?
How important is tooling and ecosystem at launch?
What is the effect of corporate or institutional backing?
How does syntax and learning curve affect adoption?
What historical examples show adoption patterns?
key_findings: Platform lock-in is the strongest single predictor (JavaScript/browser, Swift/iOS, Kotlin/Android)
Ecosystem grows adoption but rarely starts it
Corporate backing accelerates but does not guarantee (Dart vs TypeScript)
Learning curve matters more for hobbyist than professional adoption
known_answer.likely_contradiction: ecosystem importance vs platform lock-in answers may appear contradictory — ecosystem is effect, not cause

observe: Did the model produce sub-questions with specific, distinct answers? Did it catch the ecosystem-vs-platform distinction in cross-check? Does the key insight identify platform dependency as the root cause?
